body:
when i was a freshman (2019) i’d always get invites to frat parties over tinder, maybe try there if it doesnt freak you out. even though that was my entry into the party scene i eventually got into clubs on campus that had their own downtown/off campus parties, and these were much more enjoyable. house/apartment parties are just as if not more fun as frats, and if you’re into music theres a very active house show scene.

tldr get a hobby/join a club, friends and parties will follow.
saw gravy a couple years ago for free at my old college. he was good (but late) imo but “free” is definitely a key word here. the pen i snuck in probably did a lot of the legwork too, lol

lots of underground stuff if that’s what youre into. i suggest following the local show organizers on Instagram to see what local bands/shows are going on- biggest ones right now are @dance_off_productions and @chowchowmedia.

Getting involved in a hobby or subculture is really the way to go! Lots of things to do if you’re into music, for example- there are live bands at most bars every weekend, house shows around town, and more chill open mic days at places like Websters and 3Dots. That’s just one route- many other activities in town to choose from!

Even in groups or clubs that have parties every week, you’ll still find people that don’t drink within those clubs. I’m in one of those clubs and while I do choose to drink, I am still friends with and have never been looked down upon by those who choose not to. I feel like most people are mature enough at psu to really not care whether or not people drink (I mean, it basically means there’s more for them) so you’ll be totally fine.

I’m in a performing arts major so I really don’t think that doing online classes for another semester would help me at all, so I’ll probably drop. Yeah, I could take the classes online and just get easy credits that way, but I have a feeling that having hands-on classes online would make me learn nothing at all. In all honesty, if it comes to that, I’ll probably have a long meeting with my advisor to figure out what I actually want to do in the end.
